NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The proposed intervention is to modify the photovoltaic module's glass composition by incorporating a sodium-blocking interlayer that prevents sodium ion migration under high-voltage bias. Standard practice relies on using low-sodium glass and edge sealing to contain sodium, but this approach fails when sodium ions migrate through the bulk glass. Our mitigation introduces a novel electrochemical barrier layer that creates an energy barrier for sodium ion migration, which standard practice does not employ. The closest existing practice is the use of barrier coatings in architectural glass to reduce UV transmission, but our approach differs by specifically targeting ion migration through electrochemical repulsion rather than physical blocking.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is Fick's first law of diffusion: J = -D(dC/dx), where J is the flux of sodium ions, D is the diffusion coefficient, and dC/dx is the concentration gradient. Our intervention introduces an electrochemical barrier layer that creates an opposing electric field to reduce the effective driving force for sodium migration. The magnitude verification shows that a 0.5 eV energy barrier reduces the diffusion coefficient D by approximately 10^5 times at operating temperatures (based on the Arrhenius equation), which would reduce annual power loss to below 0.5% over 25 years.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard practice components:
- Low-sodium cover glass (a)
- Ethylene-vinyl acetate (EVA) encapsulant (a)
- Aluminum frame (a)
- Junction box with bypass diodes (a)
- Tedlar backsheet (a)

Proposed intervention components:
- Low-sodium cover glass (a) [existing component retained]
- Sodium-blocking interlayer (b) - commercially available ion-blocking coating used in battery separators
- Modified EVA encapsulant with increased adhesion promoters (b) - standard product with formulation change
- Aluminum frame with enhanced edge sealing (c) - configuration change to improve sealing at interlayer interface
- Junction box with bypass diodes (a) [existing component retained]
- Tedlar backsheet (a) [existing component retained]

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Glass: Same (a) - no change to existing component
- Encapsulant: Same class (b) - standard product with formulation change, no new equipment
- Interlayer: New (b) - procurable standard product from battery industry
- Frame: Same class (c) - configuration change only, no new hardware
- Junction box: Same (a) - no change
- Backsheet: Same (a) - no change
- Installation procedure: Same (a) - no additional steps required
- Testing procedure: Same (a) - uses existing qualification tests

Burden class: Same - all changes use existing infrastructure or procurable standard products with no new equipment required.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Subject modified and control modules to 1000 V bias at 85°C/85% relative humidity for 1000 hours (IEC 61215 qualification test with extended duration). Measure power output at 0, 250, 500, 750, and 1000 hours. After testing, perform electroluminescence imaging and I-V curve analysis to detect shunting paths.

Instruments: Solar simulator, temperature/humidity chamber, high-voltage power supply, data acquisition system.

Pass/fail threshold: Modified modules must show less than 0.1% power loss after 1000 hours of testing, while control modules (standard practice) must show greater than 0.5% power loss.

Duration: 1000 hours of accelerated aging testing.

Kill criterion: If modified modules show power loss exceeding 0.2%, the intervention fails. If control modules show less than 0.3% power loss, the test is invalid due to insufficient stress.
